title: C
body:
The language from [[INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTER SCIENCE 2]], and the reason this course exists:
C is thin enough that almost every construct in it maps onto something you can now point at.

| In C | On the machine |
|---|---|
| [[Pointer]] | an address in an address register, dereferenced by [[Addressing Modes\|register indirect]] |
| [[Data type]] | how many bytes and how to read them, see [[Data representation]] |
| [[Type casting]] | reinterpreting bits that never moved |
| local variables | offsets from the stack pointer, see [[Subroutines]] |
| `&&`, `\|\|` | a compare and a branch, see [[Status Bits]] |
| `x << 3` | `lsl.l #3`, see [[Binary Operations]] |

Compiling a C function and reading the [[Assembly]] the compiler emitted is the fastest way
to check you understand either one.
